idea: Why a toilet may keep running
title: Why Is Your Toilet Running Non-Stop?
description: A running toilet isn’t just an annoying sound—it can waste hundreds of gallons of water each day. The root cause is almost always inside the cistern. Most frequently, a worn or warped rubber flapper fails to create a tight seal at the bottom of the tank, allowing water to constantly leak into the bowl. Another common cause is a misadjusted float arm or fill valve, which lets water rise too high and continually spill over the top of the overflow tube. Checking these two internal components is the best place to start troubleshooting before calling a professional plumber.
image_prompt: A crisp, photorealistic vertical commercial photograph taken from a top-down angle looking directly inside an open ceramic toilet cistern in a modern residential bathroom. The white porcelain tank lid has been carefully removed. The water inside the tank is clear, fully exposing the internal plumbing components: a vertical fill valve assembly, a float cup, a flexible fill tube, a vertical overflow pipe, and a black rubber flapper resting over the flush valve seat with a stainless steel chain attached. Water is visibly touching the exact upper rim of the open overflow tube, clearly demonstrating how a high water level flows endlessly into the overflow pipe. The scene is softly lit with natural daylight reflecting off the clean water surface and porcelain walls. Shot on a 50mm lens with f/2.8 depth of field, sharp focus on the overflow tube rim and water line, smooth realistic textures, photorealistic ceramic and plastic materials, no hands, no text, no visual graphics.
